title: Reliability Sprint Conductor — Cadence, Integration, and Team Protocols
content:
Purpose
This doc captures an experimental cross-functional cadence I want to run for the next 90 days to drive SLO alignment, faster oncall handoffs, and clearer integration points between Product, Serving Runtime, Platform, and SRE. Think of this as a lightweight "conductor" pattern: one person (the conductor) runs a weekly tempo, coordinates small surgical touchpoints, and triages dependency work into a 30/60/90 sprint backlog.

Context and why this feels needed
- We've historically had long-running SLO conversations that stall between Product (requirements), Platform (capacity), and Serving Runtime (implementation).
- When incidents happen, the handoff to Product and postmortem actioning is inconsistent.
- We need a repeatable, low-cost ritual that keeps SLO decisions moving without creating extra meetings.

Goals (north star)
- Move 8 SLO decisions from "needs alignment" -> "accepted and staged for rollout" in 90 days.
- Reduce mean incident handoff time (ops -> product owners) by 25%.
- Have a documented integration checklist per feature that maps to the SLOs + required observability signals.

Scope (what this conductor runs)
- SLO proposal triage and prioritization (light-weight economic/impact sizing)
- Observability signal mapping and dashboarding quickfixes (top 5 signals per SLO)
- Runbook hygiene checks and ownership consolidation for critical services
- Cross-team cutover windows & rollout safety checks (canary thresholds, fallback model variants)

Roles and commitments
- Conductor (rotating): runs the weekly tempo, owns the short list and parking lot. Week 1-4: Jordan (owner). Week 5-8: Priya.
- Stitcher: connects infra/serving changes with product acceptance tests (usually Platform or Serving engs). Current: Alex Kim.
- Ops Liaison: ensures oncall rota and escalation updates; triages incident signals into the backlog. Current: Sofia Alvarez.
- Product Gatekeeper: signs off on user-impact tradeoffs and rollout plan. Default: Marcus Li (product).
- Documentation Scribe: ensures runbooks / checklist updates land in the repo and Confluence. Evelyn O'Neill.

Weekly cadence (2–4 short rituals, ~30–60 mins total)
- Monday: Conductor's quick sync (15 min) — review the 3 highest-priority SLO items for the week, confirm owners and acceptance criteria.
- Wednesday: Integration stand (30 min) — optional deep-dive for items with infra dependencies; invite Serving Runtime and Platform leads.
- Friday: Rapid retrospective (15 min) — what moved, what blocked, escalate blockers into platform escalation channel.
- As-needed: Emergency slot (60 min) called by Ops Liaison for incident cross-team triage.

90-day milestone plan (high level)
- 0–30 days: Intake + agreement on decision criteria (latency/cost/impact). Deliverable: decision rubric + top 8 candidate SLOs prioritized.
- 31–60 days: Implementation & dashboards. Deliverable: per-SLO dashboard + runbook stub + canary plan for at least 4 SLOs.
- 61–90 days: Rollouts and retro. Deliverable: 2 live rollouts, postmortem on process, and a refined playbook.

Decision rubric (proposal, quick checklist)
- User impact: high/med/low (user-facing failure modes prioritized)
- Cost delta: estimated % token-cost change or infra cost (approx)
- Implementation effort: small (days) / medium (weeks) / large (quarters)
- Observability maturity: green/amber/red (can we measure now?)
- Rollback safety: yes/no (automatic fallback available?)

SLO intake template (use as form)
- Service name: 
- Proposed SLO (user-visible): (e.g., 99th percentile inference latency < 250ms for API responses)
- Why it matters (user story + product metric):
- Measurement signal(s): (synthetic latency, tail latency histogram, error-rate by code)
- Owner(s):
- Implementation sketch: (routing change, batching, KV cache, quantization profile)
- Approx cost impact: (ballpark)
- Rollout plan: canary %, rollback triggers, monitoring checks

Integration checklist per feature (must be green before cutover)
- SLO measurement in dashboards: yes/no
- Synthetic monitors created: yes/no
- Runbook updated with: owner, rollback steps, pager routing: yes/no
- Canary plan defined: yes/no
- Capacity buffer confirmed with Platform: yes/no
- Stakeholders notified and quiet-window scheduled: yes/no

Escalation protocol (short)
- Phase 0: Ops detects anomaly -> Ops Liaison picks up and posts to #ops-sre with severity tag.
- Phase 1: Conductor convenes emergency slot if cross-team. Immediate next steps captured in incident channel.
- Phase 2: If rollout impacts SLOs and cannot be mitigated, Product Gatekeeper signs off on temporary user-facing risk messaging and rollout pause.
- Phase 3: Postmortem owners assigned within 48 hours and actions tagged in Jira with owner and due date.

Observability and signal hygiene focus (top 5 signals across set)
- Tail latency p95/p99, per route and model variant
- Error rate by class (5xx, model-decoding errors, timeouts)
- Queue/backpressure metrics (request queue length, batching lag)
- Cache/kv hit ratio and cold-start rate
- Cost per 1k tokens / inference-unit trend (to monitor regressions)

Risk register (early capture)
- Risk: Dashboard coverage poor for legacy services. Mitigation: stitcher pairs with service owner for quick synthetic monitor (2 days).
- Risk: Platform capacity mis-estimate for canary. Mitigation: reserve small burst pool and staged traffic ramp.
- Risk: Runbook ambiguity leads to delayed handoffs. Mitigation: use a tight runbook template and require Conductor sign-off before cutover.

Artifacts and where they live
- Runbooks + checklists: ops-playbooks repo (PR template) -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks
- Decision rubric + intake form: Confluence page (linked_artifacts above)
- SLO dashboards: Grafana team folder (link added once dashboard created)

Success criteria (how we know this worked)
- Process: > 5 SLO decisions accepted and staged in 90 days.
- Operational: mean incident handoff time reduced by 25% versus baseline (measure using postmortem timestamps).
- Culture: at least 3 feature teams adopt the conductor checklist for their launches.

Open questions / parking lot
- Should the conductor be a dedicated 0.2 FTE role or rotate weekly? Pros/cons in notes below.
- How to track the handoff time metric reliably? (product tag in postmortem workflow?)
- Can we automate some of the intake measurements (cost delta) from the Optimize telemetry?

Immediate next actions (this week)
- Jordan: create intake form and add to Confluence (due 2026-01-22).
- Alex: prototype a minimal SLO dashboard template and share (due 2026-01-29).
- Priya: schedule initial stakeholder invite list and weekly slots (due 2026-01-21).
- Sofia: test emergency slot workflow with oncall team (due 2026-01-25).

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep rituals short. Avoid creating a new "big meeting" — the value is in quick unblock and action triage.
- Use a single list in GitHub issues for the conductor backlog (label: conductor/90d).
- Keep the first 4 SLOs intentionally small to demonstrate progress and unblock skeptics.

Appendix: short retrospective template for end of each 30-day window
- What moved? (deliverables shipped)
- What didn't? (blocked items)
- What surprised us?
- One thing to change next 30 days
